name: lance_file::concat::DataFilePart::open
behavior: DataFilePart::open first validates any supplied Blob range before IO, then reads all metadata, normalizes anonymous Blob descriptor children and checks optional expected rows against footer count. A mismatch is InvalidInput naming path, actual and expected, before Blob checks. Stored scheduler/metadata have no local ETag/content-hash binding or later immutability recheck. Open rejects any normalized schema field with is_blob&&!is_blob_v2 as NotSupported. It projects descriptor form and delegates exact-version complete-column/uniform-length validation; every delegated error is wrapped as CorruptFile with the input path and incomplete metadata context. Returned normalized length must equal footer rows, otherwise CorruptFile. This validates encoded metadata, not all non-Blob data values. If any schema field is Blob v2, open awaits descriptor validation before checking that target ID is Some. Thus missing target may be reported only after descriptor IO or a descriptor error. A Blob schema needs a target even if every descriptor is null/empty/external; a lease is required by managed values, not by schema alone. Successful open retains all inputs/Arcs/options unchanged; public num_rows returns metadata footer count.

name: lance_file::concat::validate_blob_descriptors
behavior: Descriptor validation builds a descriptor-projected schema, collects Blob v2 field IDs and BTreeSet uniqueness. Duplicate IDs or a negative minimum produce CorruptFile. project_by_ids(...,true) keeps structural context. Exact data_file_columns maps IDs to physical columns; zipped pairs with either negative value are dropped and remaining u32 pairs collect into BTreeMap, with later duplicate keys replacing earlier ones. Exact reader_projection_from_field_ids may fail. Descriptor validator reopens FileReader with selected projection, default DecoderPlugins/options and no cache; this is another metadata open after DataFilePart::open read_all_metadata. It streams RangeFull with8192 row batches,readahead4,no filter. Each batch allocates an all-true selection vector and recursively validates zipped Arrow fields/arrays. It decodes descriptor arrays rather than Blob payload content and does not collect the whole stream.

name: lance_file::concat::validate_blob_field
behavior: validate_blob_field handles Arrow field.is_blob first, assuming a Struct array and named primitive kind(UInt8),position/size(UInt64),blob_id(UInt32) columns. Missing names are CorruptFile; AsArray type mismatches can panic. It enumerates the supplied selection and skips unselected or null descriptor rows. No independent selection-length or child-validity check exists here; schema/Arrow construction are trusted. blob_uri is not fetched or validated. BlobKind conversion can reject unknown byte kinds. Inline with size>0 is InvalidInput; zero-size Inline is accepted without position/ID checks. Packed/Dedicated require Some lease and ID membership; Dedicated additionally requires position0 or CorruptFile. Packed offsets/sizes and managed payload existence/length are not checked, and repeated IDs within a lease are allowed. External passes without URI/base/offset/size validation. Return after handling a Blob field, without recursively validating descriptor children as ordinary fields. For ordinary Struct, intersect selected rows with parent validity, allocate a child-selection Vec<bool> and recurse through zipped children/columns. Invalid parent rows suppress checks of otherwise populated descendants. There is no explicit child-count equality check in this helper. For List(i32), allocate false flags for the complete child value array; each selected valid parent marks its offset interval true, then recurse into the values. Offset casts/range slicing trust valid Arrow invariants and can panic on inconsistent arrays or selection lengths. Null/unselected parent items remain unvalidated. LargeList repeats List propagation with i64 offsets cast to usize. All other Arrow data types take an empty branch, including FixedSizeList/Map/ListView-style containers at this local boundary. The function returns Ok after recursive validation; it has no direct tests in this file for container nulls or those unhandled shapes.

name: lance_file::concat::check_compatibility
behavior: check_compatibility first rejects any Blob in the ordinary target schema, then requires a first prepared input. It derives the baseline physical columns from the first input, descriptor-projects the target only for part mode, and serializes all baseline column encodings before checking input row/version/schema. It does not itself reject target V1; public ordinary dispatch handles legacy earlier. Per-input check order is expected footer rows(InvalidInput), exact version(Unsupported VersionMismatch), complete Schema equality(Unsupported SchemaMismatch), exact external-metadata validation(CorruptFile wrapping any delegated error), then normalized/footer row equality(CorruptFile). No coercion, alias equivalence, column reordering or semantic encoding comparison is attempted. After metadata validation, more than one global buffer gives Unsupported ExtraGlobalBuffers; schema buffer0 is regenerated. Different column count versus the first input gives ColumnLayoutMismatch(None), although prior schema/metadata checks may reject first. A zero-global buffer case has no local rejection here; valid readers normally require schema storage upstream. Each physical column must have no column-level buffers, the same index as baseline and identical serialized column-level encoding. Error order is ColumnBuffers then index layout then encoding mismatch. Different page encodings/page counts are allowed if preceding validation succeeds. Returns None after every input; it never reads page payloads or validates their absolute ranges against EOF.

name: lance_file::concat::copy_page_buffers
behavior: copy_page_buffers allocates output PageInfo capacity equal to page count and groups consecutive complete pages. For each page, checked offset+size rejects u64 range overflow and checked sum(size) rejects page byte-count overflow as contextual CorruptFile with path,input,column,page. There is no local offset+size<=file_size check; subsequent scheduler IO determines out-of-file behavior. A page after the first in a batch is deferred when checked cumulative bytes overflow or exceed read_batch_bytes. The first page is always admitted, even oversized. The aggregate addition is then checked. Buffer counts include zero lengths but read ranges omit them; positive offset+size arithmetic is safe only because the earlier checked pass succeeded. Page boundaries/order are preserved, with no sorting/coalescing here. One scheduler request at priority0 returns all positive-length ranges in the batch, or no IO occurs if none. Consume one returned Bytes per nonempty buffer; missing response or unequal byte length is contextual IO error, including overlong results under the short-read wording. Zero buffers consume no result but still call writer.write_external_buffer(empty). Each buffer is written sequentially and its new offset/size retained. After writing all buffers of each page, clone its encoding, preserve num_rows and checked-add whole-input row_offset to priority. Priority overflow is InvalidInput after possible output writes. Extra returned buffers are rejected only after the batch writes. Retain relocated PageInfo for all pages; no page decoding, retry, checksum or rollback occurs in this helper.

name: lance_file::concat::concat_prepared
behavior: concat_prepared is generic over a FnOnce async output factory. Reject zero read threshold, run compatibility, checked-sum footer row counts, and return Reused(0,metadata size) for exactly one ordinary input. This path never calls the factory or validates/uses writer_options. Part mode passes reuse_single_input=false and always creates output after checks, even for one part. After all compatibility and total-row checks, await output factory and exact create_lazy_writer. Both calls are outside the write_result async block, so an error here does not invoke the explicit writer.abort branch below. Allocate one Vec<PageInfo> per first-input physical column and row_offset0. No metadata/page count memory budget or streaming footer builder exists here. Traverse inputs in caller order and columns in metadata order, invoking exact copy_external_metadata_column with whether that output column already has pages. Its closure copies buffers and appends relocated pages. Checked row_offset advances once per input after all its columns. V2_0 dispatch may skip later structural header columns; V2_1/2/3 invoke every copy. This loop is sequential across files/columns and retains all output page metadata. Finalize each output column through exact-version hook, then create ColumnInfo with baseline index/encoding, moved accumulated pages and an empty column-buffer vector. V2_0 structural header finalization reduces to one page with total rows/priority0; other current versions leave pages unchanged. Output page encodings can remain heterogeneous. An empty external-buffer write aligns the upcoming schema descriptor. initialize_with_external_columns receives target schema clone, constructed columns and total rows; finish writes normal metadata/footer and shuts down. Success returns Written with exact target version and writer summary counts/size. Any error inside write_result awaits writer.abort then returns the original error; abort returns no Result here. There is no cancellation Drop guard, and cancellation before reaching the match does not execute this explicit abort.

Same white-box test clears normalized column_infos while preserving schema/footer, calls compatibility and asserts CorruptFile plus schema requires1physical columns substring. This tests external metadata validation before baseline column-count reasoning. Same test clones normalized pages, decrements first num_rows by1 and rebuilds ColumnInfo. check_compatibility must return CorruptFile containing descriptor reports2physical rows. name: lance_file::concat::tests::missing_and_corrupt_inputs_are_errors_without_output
behavior: Missing-input test writes valid and soon-deleted2rowV2_1 files, opens scheduler before deleting the latter, then concatenates both. Requires only is_err and factory0; no error type/message or missing-source recovery assertion. Corrupt-input test writes literal not a Lance file, shuts down and concatenates with a valid input. It asserts only is_err. Its factory itself returns Err and has no call counter, so this oracle alone does not prove the factory was never called. File ends with seven tests(one four-version matrix) and two helpers. No local decoded-payload equality, Blob descriptor/null/container, zero-threshold, single-part-write, short/extra IO, abort/cancellation or overflow tests.
